rawCommits.subject: fix(ci): pass shell:true on Windows so npm.cmd stops failing PRs with EINVAL
rawCommits.body:
Node 18.20.2+/20.12.2+/21.7.3+/22+ refuses to spawn `.cmd`/`.bat` shims
without `shell: true` (CVE-2024-27980). On Windows our parity helpers
rewrite `npm`/`npx` to `npm.cmd`/`npx.cmd`, so every Windows CI lane in
desktop-validate failed at the very first `npm ci` with
`spawnSync npm.cmd EINVAL` before the shim was ever launched. This blocked
community PRs that couldn't bypass the required Windows check.

Add a `needsShell` helper scoped to the same commands `commandName`
rewrites and pass it through to all three spawnSync sites (run, capture,
tryCapture). Keep it scoped to npm/npx so we don't opt every spawn into
shell-quoting risk; current call sites only pass simple tokens and plain
paths, which cmd.exe parses safely.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: pass shell:true on Windows so npm.cmd stops failing PRs with EINVAL

rawCommits.subject: feat(aura-os-core): extend harness_agent_id with optional session segment
rawCommits.body:
Adds a third Option<&SessionId> argument to harness_agent_id, producing
the three-segment form {template}::{instance|default}::{session_id}
when Some is passed. None preserves today's two-segment strings exactly,
so every existing call site is updated to pass None and behavior is
byte-identical at this phase.

This is phase 0 of the parallel-session-chats plan: subsequent phases
thread Some(session_id) on chat routes to give each storage session its
own harness partition, registry entry, and turn slot.

rawCommits.subject: feat(aura-os-server): partition chat sessions by storage session_id
rawCommits.body:
Threads the resolved storage session_id into the harness session_key for
both bare-agent and project-instance chat routes, so two POSTs against
the same agent instance with different session_id values now open two
distinct ChatSession entries in the registry, take two distinct
turn_slot mutexes, and stream concurrently end-to-end.

Removes the now-degenerate pin-change and auto-fork eviction blocks: with
per-session keys, the partition you look up *is* the partition for the
requested session, so eviction-on-mismatch can never fire and the new
fork session is naturally orphaned on its own key. The auto-fork
stability_metrics bump is preserved.

setup::reset_instance_session now sweeps every per-session entry under
the instance via a new prefix-match helper. setup::reset_agent_session
is unchanged; bare-template resets target a single key.

Loop, single-task, public-chat, and Swarm-tools paths intentionally stay
on the bare (template, instance|None, None) partition; the cross-feature
busy-guard via the automaton registry continues to serialize them
against chat regardless of which session_id chat targets.

Adds an integration test that two storage sessions on the same instance
stream concurrently without serialization, plus a regression case in the
existing concurrent_agents suite. Refreshes aura-protocol::SessionInit
doc comment to spell out the three-segment partition string.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: feat(interface): key chat stream lanes by session id
rawCommits.body:
Threads sessionId into the useStreamCore deps for both project chat
(use-chat-stream) and standalone agent chat (use-agent-chat-stream)
so each storage session gets its own streamKey on the client. Two
sessions of the same agent instance can now stream concurrently
without sharing isStreaming state, abort controllers, partition
send-control, or chat-ui-store entries.

Adds a migrateStreamPartition helper (and matching siblings in
partition-send-control + chat-ui-store) and wires it into
build-stream-handler.ts at both session-id flip sites: the
SessionReady branch (fresh-canvas placeholder -> real session id)
and the auto-fork progress branch (mid-stream fork -> new session
id). State carries forward correctly across both transitions.

Removes the now-obsolete cross-session leak guards in
AgentChatPanel and use-standalone-agent-chat: with per-session
streamKeys, an active stream in session A can no longer leak deltas
into session B's transcript, so the getIsStreaming(streamKey)
bail-outs were dead code.

Adds a per-session streaming indicator in SessionsList via a
useIsSessionStreaming selector keyed off the same per-session
storeKey, so the sidebar shows which sessions have a turn in
flight while you view a different session.

Phase 3 of the parallel-session-chats plan; depends on aura-os
server-side per-session lanes from f75bcb44e.

rawCommits.subject: fix(aura-os-server): repair reset_agent_session sweep + doc-comment
rawCommits.body:
After Phase 1 of parallel-session-chats, the bare-agent chat route
stores ChatSession entries at the three-segment partition string
{template}::default::{session_id}, but reset_agent_session was
still looking up the two-segment {template}::default via
remove_live_session (exact-match). The reset endpoint silently
no-op'd on every modern bare-agent chat — old sessions plus their
turn_slot mutexes leaked indefinitely.

Renames remove_live_sessions_for_instance to
remove_live_sessions_for_partition (the helper has always been
partition-shape-agnostic; the "instance" naming was misleading after
Phase 1 made it usable for bare partitions too) and re-targets both
reset endpoints at it. The == branch covers the legacy two-segment
form so callers that opted out of the session segment are still
swept; the starts_with branch covers every three-segment per-session
entry under that partition. The now-dead exact-match
remove_live_session helper is removed.

Also refreshes the ChatSessionKey.session_key doc comment in
state/mod.rs to spell out the three-segment shape; Phase 1 changed
the structure but never updated the comment.

rawCommits.body:
Tightens the chat session id chain from String to the typed
aura_os_core::SessionId newtype at the in-memory layer:

  * ResolvedChatSession.session_id, ChatPersistCtx.session_id, and
    both ForkInfo session-id fields are now SessionId.

(JSON), aura_os_storage::CreateSessionEventRequest.session_id, the

IPC), and aura-protocol shapes are all unchanged. The route handlers

plumbing, and stringify once at egress.

347751e25): with session_id already SessionId, build_chat_partition
calls harness_agent_id directly without the parse step. Closes the

rawCommits.subject: refactor(interface): unify partition auto-retry state across chat surfaces
rawCommits.body:
Project chat (useChatStream) and standalone agent chat
(useAgentChatStream) used to maintain two independent module-level
Maps for the same conceptual state — per-partition retry budget,
in-flight latch, lastSendArgs / lastUserContent replay payload, and
retry timer handle. The migration orchestrator had to know about
both individually, and the standalone surface hand-rolled its own
rekey block inside migrateToSession.

This commit consolidates both into a single
hooks/stream/partition-state module that owns
partitionSendControlMap (project chat) and partitionAgentReplayMap
(standalone agent), exposes a unified migratePartitionAutoRetry
helper, and keeps the per-surface field shapes that legitimately
differ (project chat tracks pendingSpec/Task placeholders + the
abort controller; standalone tracks the user-content replay
payload). The migration orchestrator now calls one helper for
auto-retry state instead of two.

No runtime behavior change; this is a pure structural cleanup
ahead of the Tier 3 item 10 PartitionRegistry abstraction.

Tier 3 item 9 of the session-keying review plan.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: refactor(interface): introduce PartitionRegistry for per-key state
rawCommits.body:
Replaces the four ad-hoc per-partition module-level Maps + their
hand-written migrate/clear helpers with a single PartitionRegistry
abstraction in hooks/stream/partition-registry.ts. Each per-partition
map registers a {name, migrate, clear} record at module load; the
migration orchestrator (migrateChatPartition) and the prune sweep
both iterate the registry list instead of calling each helper by
name.

Concrete registrations:

  * "stream-entries"           - useStreamStore.entries + streamMetaMap
  * "partition-send-control"   - project-chat retry/replay state
  * "partition-agent-replay"   - standalone-agent retry/replay state
  * "chat-ui-partition"        - drafts + selected mode/model + pinned
                                  source images

Adding a new per-partition map now means writing one module that
registers itself once; the orchestrator and the prune sweep pick it
up automatically. Closes the structural footgun where the Phase-3
asymmetry (standalone agent skipping migratePartitionSendControl)
was caused by remembering-to-call-each-helper at every flip site.

Existing public exports (migrateStreamPartition,
migratePartitionAutoRetry, migrateChatUiPartition, etc.) stay as
back-compat thin wrappers because the test suite imports them
directly. Zero runtime behavior change; structural refactor only.

Tier 3 item 10 of the session-keying review plan.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: refactor(aura-os-server): replace too_many_arguments cheats with config structs
rawCommits.body:
Inventories every #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)] on the chat
hot path + persistence helpers and replaces each with a borrowed
config struct (modeled on the existing OpenChatStreamArgs in
streaming.rs). Closes the suppression debt accumulated across the
parallel-session-chats work and satisfies the Rust rule that bans
the cheat.

Functions converted (and the new config struct each takes):

  * persist::resolve_chat_session_with_pin
      -> &ChatPersistRequest<'_> + &ChatSessionResolveDeps<'_>
  * setup::setup_project_chat_persistence
      -> &ChatPersistRequest<'_>
  * setup::setup_agent_chat_persistence
      -> &ChatPersistRequest<'_>  (also drops the unused _agent_name)
  * setup::setup_agent_chat_persistence_with_matched
      -> &ChatPersistRequest<'_> + &ChatSessionResolveDeps<'_>
  * agent_route::load_persistence_only
      -> &ChatPersistRequest<'_>
  * agent_route::load_history_for_agent
      -> &LoadAgentHistoryCtx<'_>
  * cross_agent_reply::run_cross_agent_reply_callback
      -> CrossAgentReplyCallbackArgs (owned; spawned task consumes
         all fields by value)
  * generation::persist::resolve_persist_ctx
      -> &GenerationPersistTargets<'_>  (the only non-chat helper
         touched; its force_new + pinned_session_id were also
         session-keying additions, so the same cleanup applies)

Two reusable structs land in chat::persist (re-exported as
ChatPersistRequest from chat::mod for image-mode generation):

  * ChatPersistRequest<'a>   – per-turn request shape: jwt,
    force_new, pinned_session_id, plus the cross-agent reply
    trio (originating_agent_id, cross_agent_depth, from_agent_id)
    that was previously threaded by hand at every call site.
  * ChatSessionResolveDeps<'a> – state-derived deps: session_service
    + chat_auto_fork_threshold, pulled off AppState by the
    handlers that already own it.

Route handlers (agent_route, instance_route) build one
ChatPersistRequest at the top of the turn and pass &request down
through persist + history loaders so the cross-agent fields can
no longer drift out of lockstep at one call site.

Pure structural cleanup; no runtime behavior change. Per-helper
diffs are mechanical (params -> struct.field). The chat handler
family now has zero #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)] entries
and the documented baseline of 9 pre-existing clippy warnings
(control.rs, sessions.rs, dev_loop/streaming/side_effects.rs,
generation/harness_stream.rs, tasks/extraction.rs) is unchanged.

Tier 3 item 12 of the session-keying review plan.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(interface): portal model picker menu so it stops being clipped by adjacent panels
rawCommits.body:
The dropdown was rendered inside the chat panel with `position: absolute`,
so the chat lane's `overflow: hidden` (and that of `.lane`, `.laneContent`,
`.mainContent`, `.mainPanelHost`, `.chatView` above it) sliced the menu
wherever it extended past the chat panel's left edge — visually reading
as if the adjacent left sidebar lane were cutting it off. Mirror the
existing `Select` pattern: render the menu through a `document.body`
portal with `position: fixed` coordinates derived from the trigger's
`getBoundingClientRect()`, so no ancestor stacking context or overflow
rule can constrain it. Adds a regression test that asserts the open
menu lives under `document.body`, not inside its `overflow: hidden`
parent.

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat): coerce non-object tool_use.input to a marker before persist
rawCommits.body:
Adds a defense-in-depth guard so a buggy or older upstream harness can
never poison the persisted assistant turn with a `tool_use.input` that
is anything other than a JSON object. Anthropic rejects such history
with 400 `messages.N.content.M.tool_use.input: Input should be an
object`, which previously silently broke every subsequent turn in the
session and required the user to restart the chat.

Changes in `apps/aura-os-server/src/handlers/agents/chat/persist_task_dispatch.rs`:
- New `coerce_tool_use_input_to_object` helper: objects pass through,
  null -> `{}`, anything else (string, array, number, bool) is logged
  at `error` and replaced with a structured `_normalized` marker that
  records the original type and byte size for forensics.
- `handle_tool_call_snapshot` now coerces the snapshot input before
  both updating the in-memory block and writing the persisted event,
  so the corruption can never round-trip through the database.
- `backfill_null_tool_use_input` is renamed to `normalize_tool_use_input`
  and broadened to catch the same non-object case at the
  tool_result boundary (the long-standing null backfill is preserved).

Changes in `conversions/session_history/in_flight.rs`:
- `apply_tool_call_snapshot` mirrors the same normalization when
  rebuilding an in-flight turn from already-persisted events, so even
  sessions saved by an older harness build replay cleanly after refresh.

Adds 9 unit tests in `persist_task_dispatch` covering the object/null/
string/array cases plus the existing append/update flow, and a
regression test in `conversions/tests/in_flight.rs` that round-trips a
persisted string-typed snapshot through reconstruction and asserts the
emitted ToolUse input is a JSON object carrying the normalization
marker.

Pairs with aura-harness fix(compaction) 63db417 which stops the
upstream `truncate_messages_for_storage` from stringifying oversized
tool_use inputs in the first place.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: coerce non-object tool_use.input to a marker before persist

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat): arm new-chat pin on the fresh-canvas partition
rawCommits.body:
After the per-session stream lane refactor, `useFreshCanvas.newChat()`
wrote `nextSendStartsNewSession` to the partition keyed by the panel's
current session id, then dropped `?session=` from the URL. The next
send fired on the `:fresh` partition and read `false` — so the wire
flag became `new_session=false`, the server reused the existing
session via `existing_session_for_agent`, `SessionReady` snapped the
URL back, and `generate_session_title` skipped because the user
message was no longer the first in the storage session. User-visible
symptoms: "+ New chat" reverted to a previous chat and the new chat
never got a Haiku-style title.

Both chat surfaces now target the lane's fresh-canvas partition key
directly so the pin lands on the partition the post-+ send actually
reads from. `useChatStream` writes to
`keyForProjectSession(projectId, agentInstanceId, null)`, and
`useAgentChatStream` writes to `keyForAgentSession(agentId, null)`
via a new per-key `nextSendStartsNewSession` field on
`PartitionAgentReplay` (replacing the per-hook ref that the previous
`core.key`-keyed reset effect had to aggressively wipe to prevent
agent-swap leaks). Both flips are covered by new regression tests
that mount with a real `sessionId`, arm the pin, rerender with
`sessionId: null`, and assert the next send POSTs `new_session=true`.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: arm new-chat pin on the fresh-canvas partition

rawCommits.subject: chore(sidekick): gated trace on setActiveTab + pin send-flow tab invariant
rawCommits.body:
Projects-app sidekick auto-flips from Sessions to Tasks when sending a
normal chat message. Repo-wide audit found only three production sites
that set `activeTab` to `"tasks"` and none of them should fire from a
normal send on the Sessions tab, so the cause is an indirect re-render
side-effect that needs a runtime stack trace to identify.

Wraps `useSidekickStore.setActiveTab` with a `console.debug` +
`console.trace` gated on `window.__AURA_DEBUG_SIDEKICK_TAB__`, matching
the existing `[aura.chatMerge]` / `[aura.cross-agent]` gated tracers in
`use-chat-history-sync`. Cost in production is a single property read.

Also pins the invariant in `sidekick-store.test.ts`: none of the store
actions invoked by a normal send (`pushTask` real + pending placeholder,
`pushSpec`, `setAgentStreaming` on and off, `patchTask`,
`notifyAgentInstanceUpdate`, `removeTask` + `clearDeletedTasks`) may
mutate `activeTab`. If a future refactor wires a tab-flip into one of
these store actions, the matching assertion breaks and the regression
is caught before it ships.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(sidekick): keep Plan-mode sends on the Sessions tab when user picked it
rawCommits.body:
Plan mode sends `action: "generate_specs"`, which `useChatStream` was
unconditionally pairing with `setActiveTab("specs")`. In the Projects
app that meant: pick the Sessions tab to follow the chat, hit send in
Plan mode, and the sidekick yanked off to Specs every single time. The
Tasks and Specs tabs sit next to each other in the sidekick (check vs
file icon) and both render vertical item lists, which is why the
symptom read as "Sessions → Tasks" — same bucket of "stop pulling me
off Sessions".

Fix: gate the auto-switch on `activeTab !== "sessions"`. Picking
Sessions is an explicit "I want to follow the chat" signal and now the
sidekick honors it. Terminal / Browser / Stats / Log / Files / Run
aren't tied to the chat stream, so the discoverability jump to Specs
is still the right call from any of them.

`clearGeneratedArtifacts()` still runs on every Plan-mode send so the
next pass doesn't mix new specs with leftovers from the previous turn.

Covered by two tests in `use-chat-stream.test.ts`:
- existing `handles generate_specs action` test now asserts the
  auto-switch only fires from a non-Sessions tab (default `terminal`)
- new regression test sets `activeTab = "sessions"`, fires a
  `generate_specs` send, and asserts `setActiveTab` is never called.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

structurally off. Tool permissions are binary on/off, so the

enforced and pinned by `system_prompt_suffix_calls_out_status_restriction`.

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat): release turn slot and cancel harness on Stop / refresh
rawCommits.body:
Pressing Stop on a chat turn — especially a long-running plan-mode
`generate_specs` turn — used to leave the per-partition turn slot
held server-side because the client only aborted its SSE reader and
no `InboundMessage::Cancel` was ever forwarded to the harness. The
warm `ChatSession` survived a refresh (`commands_tx` still open), so
the next user message blocked on `acquire_turn_slot` until the 90s
SSE idle timeout fired `SSEIdleTimeoutError` with no actionable
error surfaced. After plan-mode -> code-mode this looked like the
chat had silently wedged.

Wires up a coordinated client + server cleanup path:

- `spawn_turn_slot_release` now selects on a
  `oneshot::Receiver<HarnessCommandSender>` in addition to the
  broadcast terminal-event arm. When the SSE stream is dropped (Stop
  or refresh) the drop guard fires the oneshot, the sentinel
  forwards `HarnessInbound::Cancel`, and releases the slot. The
  `biased` select keeps the happy-path terminal-event arm winning
  when the harness ends normally.
- `streaming::open_harness_chat_stream` plumbs `commands_tx` through
  `SessionForTurn` and wraps the SSE body in `SseDropGuardStream`,
  which fires the oneshot exactly once when axum drops the response.
- New `POST /api/agents/:agent_id/cancel-turn` and
  `POST /api/projects/:project_id/agents/:agent_instance_id/cancel-turn`
  endpoints sweep every live `ChatSession` on the partition, forward
  Cancel, and evict the warm sessions so the next send cold-starts
  cleanly. Idempotent: 204 even when nothing is in flight.
- `stopStreaming` in both `use-chat-stream` and
  `use-agent-chat-stream` now POSTs the new endpoint fire-and-forget
  before the existing `AbortController.abort()`. The server-side
  drop guard is the safety net if this POST never lands.

Tests: extends the `turn_slot` suite with the new oneshot path and
adds a `setup` registry-only worker test to pin the partition-prefix
sweep + Cancel forwarding contract; the frontend gets a regression
guard that `stopStreaming` POSTs `cancel-turn` and swallows network
failures.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: release turn slot and cancel harness on Stop / refresh

rawCommits.subject: feat(dev-loop): persist harness events as SessionEvents so replays share chat's compaction pipeline
rawCommits.body:
The dev-loop now subscribes its harness event broadcast to the same
persistence pipeline the chat agent uses, via a thin sibling
spawn_dev_loop_persist_task that delegates to the existing
chat::persist_task_dispatch::handle_outbound + chat::persist_task::
persist_event machinery. Every dev-loop harness event lands as a
SessionEvent, so any future replay through
session_events_to_agent_history goes through the same dangling-tool-use
strip, recent-window cap, tool-blob truncation, and (post-G0a) parallel-
tool-result dedupe.

The sibling exists (rather than calling spawn_chat_persist_task
directly) because the dev-loop broadcast is multi-turn (one harness
session, many assistant_message_end events as the loop runs many
tasks), while spawn_chat_persist_task breaks on the first terminal
event; and because the dev-loop wire shape is broadcast::Sender<
serde_json::Value> rather than chat's typed broadcast::Sender<
HarnessOutbound>. The sibling deserializes each JSON event best-
effort to HarnessOutbound, reuses handle_outbound for the per-event
persistence dispatch, and resets per-turn accumulators at every
assistant_message_end so the next turn does not inherit the
previous turn's text / content_blocks. Chat-specific WS publishes
are funneled through a local broadcast sender whose receiver is
dropped at construction, so they never leak onto AppState::
event_broadcast where chat-only UI subscribers would treat them as
live chat traffic.

The change is additive: the existing dev-loop side-effects worker,
loop_log writer, and LoopHandle progress updates are unchanged. The
persist task is a second consumer of the same broadcast.

Part of the fix dev-loop progress signal plan (Phase G0b / F1).

rawCommits.body:
Introduces three resilience improvements on top of the new
aura-os-automation crate:

- automation::failure::synthesize_failure_reason produces a fallback
  reason string when the harness emits task_failed without one; the
  reason is persisted to Task.execution_notes so the UI no longer
  shows silent failures.
- automation::resilience::ToolRetryTracker gates tool_call_failed
  retries at TOOL_CALL_RETRY_BUDGET (8) and emits a task_retrying
  signal while under budget, then falls through to the failure path.
- automation::resilience::TaskRetryTracker gates task-level retries at
  TASK_LEVEL_RETRY_BUDGET (3); when under budget the dev-loop uses
  aura_os_tasks::safe_transition to push Failed -> Ready so the
  scheduler picks the task up again.
- automation::resilience::recover_orphans sweeps for InProgress tasks
  at loop start and returns a plan the dev-loop applies via
  safe_transition so loops killed mid-run resume cleanly.

dev_loop/streaming/side_effects.rs gains the wiring at the
task_failed and tool_result arms; the file is not yet split (G3b/G5
covers the split). dev_loop/start.rs gains a recover_orphans call
before the scheduler starts.

(Phase G3a / Sections B, D, E).

rawCommits.subject: feat(automation): scaffold task_context resolver and exploration budget for dev-loop F2/F5 (server wiring deferred)
rawCommits.body:
Land the pure Domain-layer pieces of Phase G4a (Sections F2 + F5)
inside `aura-os-automation`. Server wiring is intentionally not
included in this commit because the existing `get_task_context`
tool and the "STRONG WARNING" exploration-budget block both live
in the out-of-tree harness binary, not in `aura-os-server` — see
the blocker note below for the bridging work that needs the harness
side first.

- aura-os-automation::task_context::TaskContextResolver caches the
  pure-built `TaskContext` payload by `(TaskId, task_version)` so
  consecutive calls within a run skip storage. The pure builder
  takes a pre-fetched `&Task` plus parent + children references and
  optional spec body, fills `title`, `description`, `spec`, `status`,
  immediate `parent` / `children` (typed `TaskRef`s), recent
  `execution_notes` truncated to 1024 characters with a leading `…`
  sentinel, and the `task_version` stamp. The cache is a bounded
  `IndexMap` keyed for FIFO eviction at 128 entries, behind a small
  `TaskFetcher` trait so unit tests stub the fetch closure.
- aura-os-automation::budget::exploration::ExplorationBudget scales
  a soft / hard pair from `description_len + dependency_count` via
  `for_task`, clamped into `[EXPLORATION_SOFT_FLOOR=8,
  EXPLORATION_SOFT_CEILING=32]` with `hard = soft * 3`. The
  `classify` verdict drives the new `advisory_text` helper, which
  emits "Heads up:" framing inside the soft band and the
  budget-exceeded escalation past the hard ceiling. Neither variant
  uses the `STRONG WARNING:` prefix the harness ships today.

Both modules ship with colocated unit tests (13 task_context, 8
exploration) covering cache hit/miss, version invalidation, FIFO
eviction, blank-spec / whitespace-notes pruning, the truncation
ellipsis, advisory tone for each `ExplorationStatus` variant, and
the floor / ceiling clamps. All 64 automation tests pass; the
existing 56 server `dev_loop` tests are unchanged and still pass.

Blocker (server wiring deferred): the `get_task_context` tool is
registered and dispatched by the harness binary (visible in
`infra/evals/local-stack/.runtime/...` payload fixtures, registered
with an empty input schema and an empty result body), and the
"hard limit: ~18 exploration calls" advisory is baked into the
harness's system prompt template. There is no server-side handler
to wire to today, and the user's instructions explicitly forbid
touching `crates/aura-os-harness/**` in this phase. The pure
helpers landed here are the right shape for the eventual bridge —
either a new control-plane callback the harness invokes for
`get_task_context` or a server-side budget header the harness
already forwards into the system prompt — and unblock that work
as soon as the harness side gains the entry point.

Part of the fix dev-loop progress signal plan (Phase G4a / Sections F2, F5).

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat): treat tool_call_snapshot mid-stream strings as the streaming protocol, not corruption
rawCommits.body:
The aura-protocol ToolCallSnapshot.input field carries Anthropic's
input_json_delta accumulator — a Value::String that grows byte-by-byte
across many small chunks until the closing brace arrives and the final
snapshot lands as a Value::Object. The previous normalize logic flagged
every intermediate snapshot as upstream corruption, spamming the error
log with one ERROR per partial chunk (the live log showed sizes
2 -> 9 -> 11 -> 16 -> 27 -> 39 -> 51 -> 60 -> 70 -> 79 for one tool_use)
and persisting throwaway _normalized placeholders to the SessionEvent
stream on every step.

- persist_task_dispatch::normalize::coerce_tool_use_input_with_status
  now classifies Value::String as the streaming case: tries to parse it
  as JSON; if a complete object lands, uses it as the canonical input;
  otherwise returns a {} placeholder + is_streaming=true and logs at
  trace (not error). The ERROR path is reserved for Array/Number/Bool,
  which Anthropic never emits for tool input.
- persist_task_dispatch::tool::handle_tool_call_snapshot returns early
  when is_streaming=true, skipping both the content_blocks mutation and
  the persist_event write. The final snapshot still lands normally, so
  end state is identical; live UI is unaffected because SSE consumers
  read directly from the harness broadcast.
- agents::conversions::session_history::in_flight::apply_tool_call_snapshot
  parses complete-object string snapshots through; unparseable strings
  (legacy historical data only — post-fix persistence never writes them)
  keep the existing _normalized marker so forensics are preserved.

Validation: cargo fmt clean; cargo clippy -p aura-os-server clean
against the post-G5b baseline (8 lib + 10 lib-test + 2 integration
warnings, all pre-existing); cargo test -p aura-os-server --lib runs
600 passed / 0 failed (was 591 baseline + 9 new regression tests).

rawCommits.body:
The dev-loop forwarder's `task_started` handler only wrote
`automaton_registry.current_task_id` (which powers the legacy
`/api/loops/status` poll endpoint) and never pushed the typed
`TaskId` onto `LoopActivity.current_task_id`. The frontend's per-task
spinner in `TaskList` binds via `selectTaskActivity(state, taskId)`,

turned off when it wasn't)" — that's this bug.

new `SideEffectCtx` bundle and updates `common::set_current_task` to
also call `LoopHandle::set_current_task(parsed)` so the typed task
id lands on the next `LoopActivityChanged` broadcast. Non-UUID
synthetic ids (`runner-<n>`) clear the pointer instead of binding to
a non-existent task.

the live `LoopRegistry`: post-`task_started` the activity carries the
task id; terminal events clear it; synthetic ids do not pollute the
pointer.

`#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` escape hatches on the
side-effects entry points (was already at the project's parameter

sidekick lane's configured "open" CSS width via `controls.getSize()`. When
the sidekick was collapsed, `controls.getSize()` still returned the open
width (e.g. 320), so the computed `available` overshot the real budget by
that amount and the sidekick ended up much wider than the main panel.

Measure `offsetWidth` on the main panel host AND a new ref to the sidekick
lane DOM, then split that combined visible budget in half. Preserve the
current outer-vs-CSS-width delta so the math is correct under either
`box-sizing` setting (ZUI's base reset applies `border-box` globally, but
the delta-based form is robust either way).

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: compute sidekick split target from rendered offsetWidth on both panels

rawCommits.subject: fix(automation-bar): keep Play visible with a spinning ring while the loop runs
rawCommits.body:
Replacing the Play icon with a Loader2 spinner during
`starting`/`preparing` and then dropping the spinner once `active`
arrived left a bare Play icon on a still-running loop — the user
read that as "the run is off" even when the harness was actively
working. The button title flipping from "Start" to "Resume" only
fires for the explicit `paused` branch, so the rest of the time the
affordance looked idle.

Keep the Play glyph rendered at all times and overlay an absolutely-
positioned SVG progress ring around it whenever the loop is doing
work (`starting`, `preparing`, or `active`). The ring mirrors
`<LoopProgress>`'s geometry and cadence (~70% arc, 1.1s linear) so
loop activity reads the same wherever it surfaces. The disabled
opacity rule is selectively overridden on the active Play button so
the icon + ring stay legible (the button remains
non-interactive — clicking Start while running is meaningless — but
the visual is informational, not faded out).

Regression tests pin the new contract:
- Play icon + progress ring present while the loop is active.
- No ring when idle.
- No ring when paused, so the now-meaningful Resume affordance
  reads as a real button.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: keep Play visible with a spinning ring while the loop runs

rawCommits.subject: fix(ui): correct sidekick split math; toggle off restores default width
rawCommits.body:
Two fixes for the split-screen toggle:

1. Drop the delta correction in `computeSplitTargetWidth`. ZUI applies
   `box-sizing: border-box` globally (vendor/zui/src/styles/base.css), so
   the lane's CSS width and `offsetWidth` are already equal. The previous
   `delta = sidekickOuter - controls.getSize()` correction broke the
   collapsed-sidekick case because `sidekickOuter` is 0 while
   `controls.getSize()` still returns the open width, pushing the target
   to `budget/2 + openWidth` and making the sidekick much wider than
   half. The simple `Math.floor((mainOuter + sidekickOuter) / 2)` formula
   handles the collapsed case correctly (budget == mainOuter, target ==
   mainOuter/2 after expand).

2. Toggling split OFF now restores `DEFAULT_SIDEKICK_WIDTH` (320) and
   persists it, instead of restoring whatever the user had drag-resized
   to previously. Both toggle states are now deterministic defaults:
   ON = 50/50 of the current main+sidekick area; OFF = the standard 320px
   sidekick width.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: correct sidekick split math; toggle off restores default width

rawCommits.subject: feat(automation): surface model selector in Run pane header too
rawCommits.body:
The previous commit only wired the model picker into the `AutomationBar`
inside `SidekickHeader`, but the Run tab inside the sidekick (the
`TaskOutputPanel`'s `RunSidekickPane`) ships its own inline
Run/Pause/Stop controls and that's where users actually expect the
model picker to live alongside the run controls. Both surfaces now
share the same per-project `automation-loop-store` slot via
`useAutomationModel`, so changing the model from either bar keeps
the other in sync and the next `startLoop` reflects the user's
latest pick from whichever surface they used.

Picker is locked once the loop is starting / preparing / active /
paused, mirroring the AutomationBar copy so neither surface can
pretend to swap the model mid-run.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: surface model selector in Run pane header too

rawCommits.subject: fix(sidekick): keep Play icon visible on Run tab with a progress-ring overlay
rawCommits.body:
The Run tab in `SidekickTaskbar` previously swapped its icon when
the loop was active — `<Play>` → `<LoopProgress>` (a 16px circle
with a faint background ring and a thin spinning arc). At
tab-strip scale that reads as "some indicator", not "the Run/Play
button, currently running": users repeatedly reported they could
no longer find the Run button after starting a live loop, and a
still screenshot of the tab strip just shows a circle wedged
between Stats (BarChart3) and Log (ScrollText).

Apply the same fix we already use for the AutomationBar's Play
button (commit `148dbe20d`): keep the Play glyph rendered at all
times and overlay a rotating progress ring when the loop is
active. The affordance stays recognisable, the ring still
communicates "currently doing work", and the Run tab no longer
disappears into a generic spinner.

- `TabIconWithProgressRing` helper added inline to
  `SidekickTaskbar.tsx`. Ring geometry mirrors the AutomationBar
  overlay (20×20 viewBox, ~70% arc, 1.1s linear infinite spin,
  accent stroke), and the ring SVG still carries
  `aria-label="running"` so existing tests that locate the
  spinner by label continue to work.
- `Sidekick.module.css` gets `.tabIconWithProgressRing` +
  `.tabProgressRing` + a `@keyframes spinTabRing` keyframe
  (separate from the existing `spinRing` keyframe in the same
  module, which is owned by `.stopRing` and rotates 0→360°).
- `SidekickTaskbar.test.tsx`:
  - Refactored the loop-store seed into a `setRunningLoop()`
    helper to keep the three new tests legible.
  - Added "keeps the Play glyph visible and overlays a ring while
    the loop is active".
  - Added "no progress ring while the loop is idle".
  - Added "no progress ring once the loop reaches a terminal
    status (completed)".

All four `SidekickTaskbar` tests pass; `tsc --noEmit` is clean.
The three pre-existing failures in `Sidekick.test.tsx` (lazy-load
pane tests) are unrelated and reproduce on `main` without this
change.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: keep Play icon visible on Run tab with a progress-ring overlay

rawCommits.subject: fix(dev-loop): surface harness stop failures instead of silently lying
rawCommits.body:
When the harness `POST /automaton/:id/stop` request failed (harness
unreachable, wrong url, non-success response), the failure was buried
in a `warn!` log and the OS-side registry was cleared anyway, so the
UI optimistically returned to idle while the harness automaton kept
running. This made "UI says stopped but harness is still going"
effectively invisible.

For Stop specifically, log the failure at `error!` with
`harness_base_url` and the error string, and forward the error in the
`loop_stopped` domain event payload as `harness_error` so the
streaming debug log (and any UI toast wired to it) makes the state
divergence visible.

Preserves the intentional "clear local registry even when harness is
unreachable" contract (see `loop_stop_clears_registry_even_when_
harness_unreachable`) so the UI can still recover when the harness is
genuinely dead.

Existing `loop_stop` tests still pass; payload shape is additive
(extra `harness_error` field on failure, unchanged `{}` on success).

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: surface harness stop failures instead of silently lying

rendered.title: Parallel chat sessions, dev-loop resilience, and sidekick controls
rendered.intro: A heavy nightly: two storage sessions on the same agent can now stream concurrently end-to-end, the dev-loop gained synthesized failure reasons, retry budgets, and orphan/Failed task recovery, and the sidekick picked up a split-screen toggle, automation model picker, and a more honest "still running" Play affordance. Windows CI was also unblocked for community PRs.

entries.title: Parallel session chats land end-to-end
entries.summary: Two storage sessions on the same agent instance can now stream concurrently, with per-session partitions on the server, per-session stream lanes in the UI, and a unified PartitionRegistry for per-key state.

items.text: Chat sessions are now partitioned by storage session_id on the server, giving each session its own ChatSession entry, turn slot, and concurrent stream; harness_agent_id grew an optional session segment and SessionId is now typed end-to-end through the persistence chain.

The interface now keys chat stream lanes by sessionId for both project and standalone agent chat, with migration helpers that carry state across the fresh-canvas→real-session flip and mid-stream auto-fork, plus a per-session streaming indicator in SessionsList.

A new PartitionRegistry consolidates per-key client state (stream entries, send-control, agent-replay, chat-ui drafts) so every partition map migrates and prunes in lockstep, closing the asymmetry that caused earlier parallel-session bugs.

Server-side chat helpers shed their too_many_arguments suppressions in favor of borrowed config structs, dedupe partition construction, restore the warm-session skip on the bare-agent route, and document shared-workspace caveats in a dedicated PARALLEL_SESSIONS.md.
Two unrelated UI fixes ship alongside: newly created projects now appear at the top of the left menu, and the model picker menu is portalled to document.body so adjacent panels can no longer clip it.
Windows CI lanes that were failing with spawnSync npm.cmd EINVAL on every community PR now pass shell:true for npm/npx shims, unblocking the required Windows check.

entries.title: Guard against non-object tool_use.input poisoning chat history
entries.summary: A defense-in-depth normalizer prevents a buggy upstream harness from persisting tool_use.input as anything but a JSON object, which previously caused Anthropic 400s that broke every subsequent turn until the user restarted the chat.

items.text: tool_use.input snapshots are now coerced to a JSON object before persistence and again at replay reconstruction; null becomes {}, anything else is logged and replaced with a structured _normalized marker carrying the original type and size.

entries.title: Dev-loop progress signal: recovery, retries, and Stop that actually stops
entries.summary: A multi-part overhaul of the dev-loop spanning a new aura-os-automation crate, real Stop/refresh cancellation, history compaction fixes, and structural splits of the oversize chat and dev-loop server modules.

items.text: Pressing Stop or refreshing now POSTs a new cancel-turn endpoint and forwards HarnessInbound::Cancel via an SSE drop guard, so the per-partition turn slot is released and the warm ChatSession evicted — fixing the wedge where the next send blocked for 90s on an SSE idle timeout.

A new aura-os-automation crate now owns the dev-loop's pure logic: classifiers, retry budgets, synthesized task-failure reasons, ToolRetryTracker/TaskRetryTracker, orphan InProgress recovery, and a task_context resolver with a complexity-scaled exploration budget.

The dev-loop spinner stall is repaired by moving loop-activity mapping into automation::progress against canonical event-kind constants, with a test-only invariant that pins the harness's event-kind names byte-for-byte.

Chat history replay is hardened: duplicate tool_result blocks for the same tool_use_id are deduped (last-write-wins) to stop Anthropic 400s, and dev-loop harness events are now persisted as SessionEvents through the same compaction pipeline as chat so replays share dangling-tool-use stripping and truncation.

Sidekick stops yanking users off the Sessions tab: Plan-mode sends only auto-switch to Specs from non-Sessions tabs, a debug-gated trace was added for stray setActiveTab calls, and the new-chat pin is now armed on the fresh-canvas partition so "+ New chat" actually starts a new titled session.

Several smaller chat polish fixes: untouched agents now restore the last-picked model instead of reverting to Sonnet, ListBlock's header was realigned with SpecBlock so the hover copy icon stops overlapping the count, the pinned cooking indicator gained a backdrop, Delete Spec / session summary no longer 400 on optimistic placeholders, and the agent picker dismisses on first click while auto-adding a Standard Agent to new projects.
Plan mode now exposes create/update/delete/transition_task so the planner can organize work without starting it, with the no-transition-to-in-progress rule pinned in the system-prompt suffix.

Behavior-preserving splits break the oversize chat (agent_route, instance_route, persist, persist_task, streaming, compaction_tests), dev-loop (side_effects, adapter, signals, start), and harness automaton_client modules into focused submodules under the 500-line cap, with public import paths preserved.

entries.title: Streaming tool_use.input is no longer logged as corruption
entries.summary: The previous normalize logic flagged every intermediate tool_use snapshot as corruption, spamming ERRORs and writing throwaway _normalized placeholders for every partial chunk. The streaming protocol is now recognized.

items.text: Mid-stream Value::String tool_use inputs are now treated as Anthropic's input_json_delta accumulator: parsed when complete, otherwise returned as a {} placeholder at trace level, and the partial snapshot is skipped from persistence so the final snapshot is the only one written.

entries.title: Sidekick gains split-screen, automation model picker, and a live Play affordance
entries.summary: The desktop shell picked up a 50/50 split toggle for the sidekick lane, the automation loop now has a deliberate per-project model selector surfaced in two places, and the Run/Play buttons keep their glyph with a progress ring overlay while a loop is running.

items.text: A new titlebar button toggles the sidekick lane to 50/50 with the main area, tracking the target via ResizeObserver and persisting state to localStorage; toggling off restores the standard 320px width and dragging the handle exits split mode cleanly.

Automation runs now use a deliberately picked model: AutomationBar and the Run pane share a per-project model selector backed by automation-loop-store, restricted to AURA_MANAGED_CHAT_MODELS, and locked once the loop is starting/active/paused.

The Play buttons in AutomationBar and the Run tab now keep their glyph visible with an overlaid progress ring while the loop is starting/preparing/active, fixing the "is it actually running?" confusion when a bare Play icon used to reappear on a still-active loop.

The dev-loop now re-readies cross-run Failed tasks on loop start (gated by the task-retry budget) and publishes the current TaskId onto LoopActivity so the per-task spinner in TaskList finally lights up during a live run.
InvokeProcess is now idempotently spliced into the in-memory capability bundle for dev-loop runs, so non-CEO agents stop burning turns retrying blocked `cargo check`/`cargo test` shell calls.

The pinned cooking indicator now aligns with the chat content edge and the sidekick Run/Tasks panes got matching gradient backdrops so trailing rows of streaming output no longer bleed through the shimmer.

entries.title: Surface harness Stop failures instead of pretending it worked
entries.summary: When the harness Stop request failed, the UI optimistically returned to idle while the automaton kept running. The divergence is now visible.

items.text: Failed harness Stop calls are now logged at error with the base URL and forwarded in the loop_stopped payload as harness_error, so the streaming debug log and any wired UI toast can show "UI says stopped, harness is still going"; the existing contract of clearing the local registry even when the harness is unreachable is preserved.

highlights: Parallel per-session chat lanes, client + server
Dev-loop now recovers orphan and Failed tasks across runs
Sidekick split-screen toggle and automation model picker
Windows CI unblocked for community PRs
Stop button actually cancels the harness turn
